front: Je pense, donc je suis.
pronunciation: [zhuh PAHNS, dunk zhuh SWEE]
back: I think, therefore I am.
context: Descartes, 'Discours de la méthode' (1637). The foundation of modern rationalism.

front: Il est cartésien jusqu'au bout des ongles.
pronunciation: [ee leh kar-tay-ZYAN zhüs-koh boo day ZOHN-gluh]
back: He's rational to his fingertips.
context: 'Cartésien' = logical, methodical. The French like to see themselves this way.

front: Le cœur a ses raisons que la raison ne connaît point.
pronunciation: [luh KUHR ah say reh-ZOHN kuh lah reh-zohn nuh koh-neh PWAN]
back: The heart has its reasons that reason knows nothing of.
context: Pascal, 'Pensées' (1670).

front: L'homme n'est qu'un roseau, mais c'est un roseau pensant.
pronunciation: [LUM neh kan roh-ZOH, meh seh tan roh-zoh pahn-SAHN]
back: Man is only a reed, but he is a thinking reed.
context: Pascal: human frailty and dignity in one image.

front: Que sais-je ?
pronunciation: [kuh SEHZH]
back: What do I know?
context: Montaigne's motto of skepticism. Also the name of a famous series of short pocket books.

front: L'homme est né libre, et partout il est dans les fers.
pronunciation: [LUM eh nay LEE-bruh, ay par-too ee leh dahn lay FEHR]
back: Man is born free, and everywhere he is in chains.
context: Opening of Rousseau's 'Du contrat social' (1762).

front: Il faut que le pouvoir arrête le pouvoir.
pronunciation: [eel foh kuh luh poo-VWAHR ah-ret luh poo-VWAHR]
back: Power must check power.
context: Montesquieu, 'De l'esprit des lois' (1748): the separation of powers.

front: L'existence précède l'essence.
pronunciation: [leg-zees-TAHNS pray-sed leh-SAHNS]
back: Existence precedes essence.
context: Sartre's summary of existentialism: we exist first, then define ourselves by our choices.

front: L'enfer, c'est les autres.
pronunciation: [lahn-FEHR, seh lay ZOH-truh]
back: Hell is other people.
context: From Sartre's play 'Huis clos' (1944): we are trapped by others' judgment of us.

front: On ne naît pas femme : on le devient.
pronunciation: [ohn nuh neh pah FAM : ohn luh duh-VYAN]
back: One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman.
context: Simone de Beauvoir, 'Le Deuxième Sexe'.

front: Je me révolte, donc nous sommes.
pronunciation: [zhuh muh ray-VOLT, dunk noo SUM]
back: I rebel, therefore we exist.
context: Camus, 'L'Homme révolté' (1951): revolt creates human solidarity.

front: Je ne suis pas d'accord avec vous, mais je me battrai pour que vous puissiez le dire.
pronunciation: [zhuh nuh swee pah dah-KOR ah-vek VOO, meh zhuh muh bah-treh poor kuh voo pwee-syay luh DEER]
back: I disagree with you, but I'll fight for your right to say it.
context: Always attributed to Voltaire, but actually written by his biographer Evelyn Beatrice Hall in 1906.

front: Tous les lycéens passent l'épreuve de philosophie au bac.
pronunciation: [too lay lee-say-AN pas lay-pruhv duh fee-loh-zoh-FEE oh BAK]
back: All high-school students sit the philosophy exam for the baccalaureate.
context: Four hours on one question, such as 'Le travail rend-il libre ?' Its topics make the news every June.

front: Peut-on être heureux sans être libre ?
pronunciation: [puh-tohn eh-truh uh-RUH sahn zeh-truh LEE-bruh]
back: Can one be happy without being free?
context: A typical 'bac philo' question.

front: Freud a mis en lumière le rôle de l'inconscient.
pronunciation: [FROYD ah mee zahn lü-MYEHR luh rohl duh lan-kohn-SYAHN]
back: Freud highlighted the role of the unconscious.
context: Psychoanalysis remains very influential in France, partly through Lacan.

front: Je vais chez le psy une fois par semaine.
pronunciation: [zhuh veh shay luh PSEE ün fwah par suh-MEN]
back: I see my therapist once a week.
context: 'Le psy' covers psychologist, psychiatrist and psychoanalyst.

front: C'est un biais de confirmation classique.
pronunciation: [seh tan byeh duh kohn-feer-mah-SYOHN klah-SEEK]
back: That's a classic confirmation bias.
context: 'Un biais cognitif' = a cognitive bias.

front: Il est en pleine dissonance cognitive.
pronunciation: [ee leh tahn plen dee-soh-nahns kog-nee-TEEV]
back: He's in the middle of cognitive dissonance.
context: Holding two contradictory beliefs at once.

front: Elle souffre du syndrome de l'imposteur.
pronunciation: [el soo-fruh dü san-drohm duh lan-pos-TUHR]
back: She suffers from impostor syndrome.
context: Feeling like a fraud despite real success.

front: Il a fait un burn-out l'année dernière.
pronunciation: [ee lah feh tan burn-OWT lah-nay dehr-NYEHR]
back: He burned out last year.
context: Official French: 'l'épuisement professionnel'.

front: La charge mentale pèse surtout sur les femmes.
pronunciation: [lah sharzh mahn-TAL pez sür-too sür lay FAM]
back: The mental load falls mainly on women.
context: The invisible work of planning a household. Popularized by the cartoonist Emma in 2017.

front: Boris Cyrulnik a popularisé la notion de résilience.
pronunciation: [boh-rees see-rül-NEEK ah poh-pü-lah-ree-zay lah noh-syohn duh ray-zee-LYAHNS]
back: Boris Cyrulnik popularized the concept of resilience.
context: The ability to recover from trauma.

front: Il manque d'estime de soi.
pronunciation: [eel mahnk des-teem duh SWAH]
back: He has low self-esteem.
context: 'L'estime de soi' = self-esteem.

front: Elle est à fleur de peau en ce moment.
pronunciation: [el eh tah fluhr duh POH ahn suh moh-MAHN]
back: She's very sensitive at the moment.
context: 'À fleur de peau' = on edge, easily hurt.

front: Arrête de te faire des films.
pronunciation: [ah-ret duh tuh fehr day FEELM]
back: Stop imagining things.
context: 'Se faire des films' = to invent scenarios in your head.

front: Je n'arrête pas de ruminer cette dispute.
pronunciation: [zhuh nah-ret pah duh rü-mee-nay set dees-PÜT]
back: I can't stop going over that argument.
context: 'Ruminer' = to brood, chew over.

front: Il faut savoir lâcher prise.
pronunciation: [eel foh sah-vwahr lah-shay PREEZ]
back: You have to learn to let go.
context: 'Le lâcher-prise' = letting go, a wellness buzzword.

front: Il n'a pas d'états d'âme.
pronunciation: [eel nah pah day-tah DAHM]
back: He has no qualms.
context: 'Avoir des états d'âme' = to have doubts, misgivings.

front: Elle a du mal à faire son deuil.
pronunciation: [el ah dü mal ah fehr sohn DUHY]
back: She's struggling to grieve.
context: 'Faire son deuil' = to grieve, come to terms with a loss.

front: Il refoule ses émotions.
pronunciation: [eel ruh-fool say zay-moh-SYOHN]
back: He represses his emotions.
context: 'Refouler' = to repress.

front: Elle culpabilise de ne pas voir assez ses enfants.
pronunciation: [el kül-pah-bee-LEEZ duh nuh pah vwahr ah-say say zahn-FAHN]
back: She feels guilty about not seeing her children enough.
context: 'Culpabiliser' = to feel guilty.

front: Il garde rancune à son frère depuis dix ans.
pronunciation: [eel gard rahn-KÜN ah sohn FREHR duh-pwee dee ZAHN]
back: He's held a grudge against his brother for ten years.
context: 'Garder rancune' = to bear a grudge.

front: La jalousie l'a rongé.
pronunciation: [lah zhah-loo-ZEE lah rohn-ZHAY]
back: Jealousy ate away at him.
context: 'Ronger' = to gnaw.

front: Il faut savoir se remettre en question.
pronunciation: [eel foh sah-vwahr suh ruh-meh-truh ahn kes-TYOHN]
back: You have to be able to question yourself.
context: 'Se remettre en question' = to be self-critical.

front: Elle a pris sur elle pour ne pas pleurer.
pronunciation: [el ah pree sür EL poor nuh pah pluh-RAY]
back: She held herself together so as not to cry.
context: 'Prendre sur soi' = to control oneself.

front: J'ai un coup de blues.
pronunciation: [zhay an koo duh BLOOZ]
back: I'm feeling a bit low.
context: 'Un coup de blues' = a passing sadness.

front: Baudelaire a donné au mot « spleen » un sens poétique.
pronunciation: [bohd-LEHR ah doh-nay oh moh SPLEEN an sahns poh-ay-TEEK]
back: Baudelaire gave the word 'spleen' a poetic meaning.
context: 'Le spleen' = deep melancholy and boredom with life.

front: La méditation de pleine conscience est à la mode.
pronunciation: [lah may-dee-tah-SYOHN duh plen kohn-SYAHNS eh tah lah MOD]
back: Mindfulness meditation is fashionable.
context: 'La pleine conscience' = mindfulness.

front: Selon Bergson, le temps vécu n'est pas le temps des horloges.
pronunciation: [suh-lohn berg-SOHN, luh tahn vay-KÜ neh pah luh tahn day zor-LOZH]
back: According to Bergson, lived time isn't clock time.
context: Henri Bergson's concept of 'la durée' (duration).

front: Foucault a analysé les rapports entre savoir et pouvoir.
pronunciation: [foo-KOH ah ah-nah-lee-zay lay rah-por ahn-truh sah-VWAHR ay poo-VWAHR]
back: Foucault analyzed the relationship between knowledge and power.
context: Author of 'Surveiller et punir' (1975).

front: Le doute est le commencement de la sagesse.
pronunciation: [luh DOOT eh luh koh-mahns-mahn duh lah sah-ZHES]
back: Doubt is the beginning of wisdom.
context: A common saying in the spirit of Descartes.

front: Connais-toi toi-même.
pronunciation: [koh-neh-TWAH twah-MEM]
back: Know thyself.
context: The Greek maxim adopted by Socrates.

front: La seule chose que je sais, c'est que je ne sais rien.
pronunciation: [lah suhl SHOHZ kuh zhuh SEH, seh kuh zhuh nuh seh RYAN]
back: The only thing I know is that I know nothing.
context: Attributed to Socrates.

front: Le bonheur est un idéal de l'imagination, pas de la raison.
pronunciation: [luh boh-NUHR eh tan nee-day-AL duh lee-mah-zhee-nah-SYOHN, pah duh lah reh-ZOHN]
back: Happiness is an ideal of imagination, not of reason.
context: Kant. A favorite quote for 'bac philo' essays on happiness.

front: Philosopher, c'est apprendre à mourir.
pronunciation: [fee-loh-zoh-FAY, seh tah-prahn-druh ah moo-REER]
back: To philosophize is to learn how to die.
context: Title of an essay by Montaigne, after Cicero.
